candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: identify medication interactions, provide administration teaching, and reduce medication-related risk.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — cholestyramine drug interactions and timing
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients taking cholestyramine to separate other oral medications by at least 1 hour before or 4–6 hours after the resin because cholestyramine can bind medications in the gut and reduce their absorption.

options.A: Take other oral medications at least 1 hour before or 4–6 hours after cholestyramine to reduce the risk that cholestyramine will impair their absorption.
options.B: Take all oral medications at exactly the same time as cholestyramine because the resin does not bind other drugs in the gastrointestinal tract.
options.C: Inject cholestyramine subcutaneously because oral administration creates clinically important drug-binding interactions.
options.D: Timing is irrelevant because cholestyramine is systemically absorbed before it can affect other oral medications.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current FDA labeling states that cholestyramine may bind other concurrently administered drugs and impede their absorption. The label recommends taking other drugs at least 1 hour before or 4 to 6 hours after cholestyramine, or at as great an interval as possible. B and D contradict this labeled interaction. C is incorrect because cholestyramine is an oral resin that acts within the gastrointestinal tract rather than being given by injection.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Cholestyramine can bind concurrently administered oral drugs and reduce absorption; current labeling recommends separating other oral medications by at least 1 hour before or 4–6 hours after cholestyramine.
candidate.source_document_title: Cholestyramine for Oral Suspension, USP Prescribing Information
candidate.source_locator: Drug Interactions/Precautions: cholestyramine may bind other drugs given concurrently. Label recommendation: take other drugs at least 1 hour before or 4 to 6 hours after cholestyramine, or at as great an interval as possible, to avoid impeding absorption. The label also notes that cholestyramine is confined to the gastrointestinal tract rather than systemically absorbed.
candidate.source_organization: U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling via DailyMed
candidate.stem: A client takes cholestyramine for hyperlipidemia and several other oral medications. Which instruction should the nurse provide?
